title: R' Yehudah ben Buni
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman says that, at the end of halakhah 1 in chapter 11 of Jerusalem Talmud Terumot, he reported in the name of R' Imi, in the name of R' Shimon ben Lakish. At the beginning of Jerusalem Talmud Bava Metzia, chapter 7: ‘Yehudah ben Buni, Rabbi Ami, Rav Yehudah: a [court] stipulation…’ Perhaps he is R' Yehudah bei R' Bun.

notes.text: The Bava Metzia name series has no explicit transmission connectors. Hyman’s identification with Yehudah bei Rabbi Bun is tentative. The source abbreviation רש״בל is rendered as Shimon ben Lakish in this context.

The saved whole Guggenheimer JerusalemTalmudBavaMetzia7:1 scalar has Yehudah ben Buni, full Rabbi Imi, full Rav Yehudah, followed by תניי בית דין. Thus supplied תני is read as the truncated beginning of stipulation rather than a verb taught; bracketed court is supplied from the named text and the full sentence is not imported. Hyman’s Ami and named Imi remain different forms; no explicit intermediate transmission links are added. The uninspected Terumot chain and possible Yehudah bei R' Bun identification remain Hyman’s, with perhaps preserved. סה״א means end of halakhah1; other abbreviated titles remain R'.

Hyman’s printed notice (vol. II, p. 555) has Yehudah ben Buni. The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 11:1 closes with Yehudah ben Keini and Rabbi Imi, followed by “in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish.” In Bava Metzia 7:1 the list has Yehudah ben Buni, Rabbi Imi, and Rav Yehudah, followed by a court stipulation. Hyman prints Ami there and abbreviates the stipulation. The differing forms are retained, and his identification with Yehudah bei R’ Bun remains tentative.
